sections.text: ## The Big Picture

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text: Development studies is the field that asks: *why are some countries rich and others poor, and what can be done about it?* It spans economics, political science, sociology, and history — and its answers have changed dramatically over 75 years of theory and practice.

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text:
```
DEVELOPMENT STUDIES LANDSCAPE

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text:
THE QUESTION
Why do living standards differ so dramatically across nations, and what are the mechanisms of change?

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text:
WHAT TO MEASURE
- GDP / GNI: income per capita (production/income)
- HDI: health + education + income composite
- MPI: multidimensional poverty (10 indicators)
- Planetary limits: are gains sustainable?

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text:
THEORY LINEAGE
1940s–60s: modernization — linear stages, Rostow, Cold War framing
1960s–80s: dependency / world systems — Frank, Wallerstein
1980s–90s: structural adjustment — Washington Consensus, IMF/World Bank
1990s–00s: post-Washington Consensus — institutions, Stiglitz; Sen capabilities
2000s–10s: RCT revolution — Banerjee/Duflo; institutional turn — Acemoglu/Robinson
2010s–: sustainability synthesis — SDGs, planetary boundaries, degrowth challenge, China model, post-development
```

sections.text: ## Measurement: GDP vs. HDI vs. MPI

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text: Three fundamentally different answers to "what is development?"

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text:
```
+-------------------+---------------------+----------------------+
|       GDP/GNI     |        HDI          |         MPI          |
+-------------------+---------------------+----------------------+
| What:             | What:               | What:                |
| Market value of   | Geometric mean of   | Headcount × intensity|
| goods & services  | 3 normalized indices| of deprivation across|
| produced          | (health, education, | 10 indicators        |
|                   | income)             |                      |
| Unit: $/person    | Unit: 0–1 index     | Unit: % × avg share  |
|                   |                     | deprived             |
| Misses:           | Misses:             | Misses:              |
| Distribution,     | Distribution within | Subjective wellbeing,|
| unpaid work,      | dimensions, beyond- | voice, capabilities  |
| sustainability,   | income poverty,     | beyond 10 indicators |
| non-market goods  | sustainability      |                      |
+-------------------+---------------------+----------------------+
| Outliers (GDP ↑): | Outliers (HDI ↑):   | Key use:             |
| Oil states (UAE,  | Kerala, Cuba (high  | Identifying who is   |
| Qatar) — high     | HDI despite low GDP)| poor and in what     |
| income, poor      | Gulf states (high   | dimension — targeting|
| human development | GDP, HDI lags)      | policy precisely     |
+-------------------+---------------------+----------------------+
```

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text: **The fundamental insight**: GDP measures income; HDI measures capabilities; MPI identifies who lacks what. They give different rankings and prescribe different policies.

sections.text: ### Debate 1: Sachs vs. Easterly — How Does Aid Work?

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text:
```
+----------------------------------+----------------------------------+
| SACHS (End of Poverty, 2005)     | EASTERLY (White Man's Burden,    |
| "The Planner"                    |  2006) "The Searcher"            |
+----------------------------------+----------------------------------+
| Poverty trap: the poor lack      | Aid creates dependency, kills    |
| investment to escape subsistence | local initiative, lacks feedback |
|                                  |                                  |
| Big push: coordinate large-scale | Markets and bottom-up searchers  |
| aid across health, education,    | find what works; top-down plans  |
| infrastructure simultaneously    | can't know local conditions      |
|                                  |                                  |
| Africa's poverty = geography +   | Africa's poverty = bad governance|
| disease burden, not institutions | + incentives warped by aid       |
+----------------------------------+----------------------------------+
| RCT synthesis: both partially    | right. Specific interventions    |
| work (CCTs, bed nets, vaccines). | Big push evidence is thin.       |
+----------------------------------+----------------------------------+
```

sections.text: ### Debate 2: Growth vs. Capabilities

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text:
```
  Growth model                     Capabilities model
  ┌──────────────┐                 ┌──────────────────┐
  │ Income → ... │                 │ Real freedoms    │
  │ purchasing   │   SEN critique: │ = ends in        │
  │ power →      │ ──────────────► │ themselves, not  │
  │ wellbeing    │ income is means,│ means to income  │
  └──────────────┘ not end itself  └──────────────────┘
                                        │
                              Agency matters: people
                              convert income differently
                              based on age, gender,
                              disability, social norms
```

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text: ### Debate 3: Institutions vs. Geography

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text:
| Factor | Sachs/Diamond position | Acemoglu/Robinson counter |
|--------|----------------------|--------------------------|
| Primary cause | Geography, disease ecology, soil quality | Colonial institutions (inclusive vs. extractive) |
| Evidence | Malaria burden correlates with poverty | Settler mortality instrument: where colonists died, they built extractive institutions |
| Policy implication | Technical fixes: bed nets, drainage | Institutional reform, democratic accountability |
| Problem | Geography predetermines outcomes (fatalist) | Endogeneity: hard to change institutions |

sections.text: ## The Institutional Turn

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text: The most influential empirical move in development economics of the 2000s–2010s: **institutions, not geography or culture, are the proximate cause of income differences.**

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text:
```
ACEMOGLU-JOHNSON-ROBINSON CHAIN (AJR 2001, 2002):

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text:
Colonial      →  Type of          →  Institutional   →  Long-run
disease          colonization         quality today       income
environment      (extractive vs.      (property rights,   (GDP/capita)
                  settlement)          rule of law)

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text:
Instrument: settler mortality (historical)
Outcome:    income today
Channel:    institutions (rule of law, property rights)

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text:
Key finding: Doubling institutional quality raises per capita income
             by 5–6× — larger effect than geography alone
```

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text: **North's formal definition**: Institutions = formal rules (laws, constitutions) + informal norms (culture, conventions) + enforcement mechanisms. Not the same as organizations.

sections.text: ## The Gender Dimension

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text: Development policy ignored women for its first four decades. The correction has been partial but substantial:

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text:
```
TIMELINE OF GENDER IN DEVELOPMENT:

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text:
1970 — Boserup: Women's Role in Economic Development
       Colonialism disrupted African women's farming → systematic marginalization
              ↓
1975 — WID: Women in Development approach
       "Add women and stir" — integrate women into existing programs
              ↓
1990s — GAD: Gender and Development
         Structural critique: transform the institutions, not just include women
              ↓
2000s — Gender mainstreaming + CCTs targeting women
         Evidence: women invest more in children's health/education
              ↓
2010s — Women's economic empowerment as growth strategy
         World Bank: "invest in women, transform economies"
```

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text: **The care economy gap**: Time-use surveys globally show women do 2–10× more unpaid care work than men. This doesn't appear in GDP, isn't compensated, and constrains women's market participation. Development policy that ignores it perpetuates the constraint.

sections.text: ## The SDGs and Planetary Limits

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text: The tension at the heart of 21st-century development:

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text:
```
THE TENSION

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text:
Development imperative:
  "Lift 700M out of extreme poverty — requires growth, energy, industrialization"

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text:
Planetary limits:
  We are already above several planetary boundaries (climate, biodiversity, P/N)

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text:
SDGs (2015–2030): 17 goals, 169 targets; comprehensiveness vs. coherence
Planetary boundaries (Rockström 2009): 9 Earth system limits, 4 already transgressed
Doughnut economics (Raworth): social foundation (SDG floor) + planetary ceiling
The space between = safe and just space for humanity
```

metadata.title: Development Studies: Growth, Human Development, Institutions - Landscape

sections.text: The **degrowth challenge** (Latouche, Kallis): is steady-state or declining GDP compatible with poverty reduction? The standard assumption — growth is necessary for development — is contested by advocates of post-growth economics.
